messages:
marta: Quick sync — ran apples-vs-replay style experiments today to chase a perf regression that shows up under autoscale + cold starts. TL;DR: when KV cache miss rate > 60% and batch size adapts up, we see kernel pivot thrash and 20-40% p95 regressions compared to steady-state. Need help validating methodology and suggestions for tighter apples-to-apples load tests.

jay: Do you have the profiler flamegraph or the pivot log? Could be the kernel selector oscillating based on sequence length distribution.

marta: Pasted a trimmed run excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:03Z] request id=rx-11 seq_len=1024 kv_hit=false batch=1 kernel=custom64 latency=120ms
[2026-03-17T14:12:03Z] request id=rx-12 seq_len=16   kv_hit=false batch=8 kernel=cudnn16  latency=45ms
[2026-03-17T14:12:04Z] kernel-selector: selected=custom64 reason="long_seq_path"
[2026-03-17T14:12:05Z] kernel-selector: selected=cudnn16  reason="short_seq_path"
[2026-03-17T14:12:06Z] autoscale: scaled_up replicas 2->4 time=48s
```
Notice the selector flips inside a 2s window causing cache warmup to re-evaluate.

alex: That scale_up time looks long for burst. What's the harness config? Synthetic harness often uses constant inter-arrival or Poisson which doesn't match replay spikes.

marta: Two harnesses used:
- replay harness: exact recorded traces from prod (prefix lengths, client think times) replayed at wallclock speed into the runtime.
- synthetic: Poisson arrivals, fixed prefix length mix (20/60/20 short/med/long).

ravi: For an apples-to-apples comparison you need to align three distributions: arrival process, prefix length distribution, and KV hit/miss model. Synthetic was underestimating rare long-prefix bursts so the selector never saw the same pivoting in synthetic runs.

kyra: Also add explicit KV cache instrumentation per-request: sample traces that include cache_key, hit boolean, and the resulting kv_latency. Right now we only log aggregate hit rate which hides bursty miss patterns.

marta: Good point. I added a per-request sampled tag for 1% of requests and saw that misses cluster at startup windows. Those clusters line up with scale-up events.

perf-bot: automated loadtest summary: 1772004287-run-1: replay x1.0 -> p95=180ms, p99=420ms; 1772004300-run-2: synthetic x1.0 -> p95=110ms, p99=260ms; scale-up latency delta=+34s vs stable.

jay: To debug kernel pivot: try forcing kernel selection via env to disable selector and run the same replay. If regression goes away, we know pivoting is the culprit. E.g. export REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=custom64 then rerun cbench.

marta: Did that: forced kernels removed oscillation but overall p95 still worse than steady-state because batching heuristics expand batch sizes aggressively when queueing spikes and that increases head-of-line latency for short requests.

alex: So it's a compound effect: (1) KV cache misses increase avg token work, (2) selector flips change kernel path performance characteristics, (3) batching increases token concurrency and amplifies variability. We should isolate each.

ravi: Suggestion: three controlled experiments with replay trace fixed:
1) fixed kernel + fixed batch cap (no adaptive batching)
2) adaptive batching + fixed kernel
3) adaptive batching + kernel selector on (full run)
Compare p95/p99 and cache warmup curves. That should quantify incremental cost.

kyra: Also measure coldstart cost separately: record time from replica launch to "ready_for_inference" and the number of warm tokens processed before cache hit ratio normalizes. We saw ~14s to ready but another ~20s to warm cache in dedicated pools.

eng-runtime-oncall: For autoscale policy: consider adding a short "warmup window" that pins batch caps for 30s after scale to avoid aggressive batch growth during cold spikes. Also consider burst credits: we've been consuming credits because autoscale spikes trigger invites to burst pool. Track burst_credit_usage metric per-replay.

marta: Action items I will run:
- add sampled per-request KV logs + cluster-aware histograms
- implement the 3 controlled experiments with the replay harness (exact arrival/prefix/hit distributions)
- force kernels for isolation runs and cap batch sizes to characterize tradeoffs
- capture scale-up timeline metrics: launch -> ready -> first_successful_kv_hit -> normalized_hit_rate
I'll push results to this thread. Any other blockers?

jay: When you push results, include the raw kernel-selector trace and a short script to replay the exact inter-arrival sequence (we can then run it on different machines to validate hardware/kernel effects).

marta: Will do. Thanks all. :pray:
